passenger jet carrying 172 people collided while taxiing at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, officials said. Two Copa passengers were assessed for apparent minor injuries, but neither needed hospital treatment.

For investors, the incident raises potential aircraft repair costs and scheduling disruptions for the carriers. The financial impact remains unknown, while airport officials said traffic was rerouted onto other taxiways without affecting overall operations.
said its Boeing 737-800 had arrived from Panama City around 9 p.m. and was heading toward the terminal when a UPS
Boeing 767 contacted its left wingtip, according to preliminary information. The UPS aircraft was preparing to depart for Bogota.
The passenger jet subsequently reached the terminal, where all 166 passengers and six crew members disembarked. Copa said it would cooperate with investigators.

The collision occurred as Miami continued dealing with delays following Friday’s nationwide ground stop. Federal officials attributed that separate disruption to overloaded air traffic control equipment that affected radar and communications. The FAA expected flight schedules to recover by late Sunday.
